Describe this histopathology image.
meta.reference: The tissue exhibits pleomorphism, large, hyperchromatic nuclei, disorganized cell arrangement, and keratin pearls, indicative of squamous cell carcinoma. Increased nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios and prominent nucleoli are noted. The stroma is infiltrated by atypical cells, showing signs of invasion and vascularization. Definitive diagnosis requires further clinical and immunohistochemical evaluation.

meta.question:

Describe this histopathology image.
meta.reference: The tissue image shows irregular glands with cribriform patterns, enlarged hyperchromatic nuclei, and absent nucleoli. The dense, fibrous stroma and lack of basal cell layer suggest prostatic adenocarcinoma. Confirmation can be made with immunohistochemistry for HMWCK and p63, which are typically negative in this carcinoma, supporting the diagnosis.
